Date: 14/01/2026
Category: Pentest | Web | Security

Tags: GraphQL
The blog page for this lab contains a hidden blog post that has a secret password. To solve the lab, find the hidden blog post and enter the password.
Link: https://portswigger.net/web-security/graphql/lab-graphql-reading-private-posts
Truy cập blog page → các bài post được load qua POST request tới /graphql/v1

Trong response, các post có ID tuần tự: 1, 2, 4, 5... → thiếu ID 3 → nghi ngờ có post ẩn với ID = 3

Post 3 bị ẩn

Trong Repeater, right-click → GraphQL > Set introspection query

Send request → response trả về full schema

Tìm type BlogPost → phát hiện field postPassword tồn tại

Trong Repeater, chuyển sang tab GraphQL
Variables panel: thay "id": 1 thành "id": 3
Query panel: thêm field postPassword vào bên trong getBlogPost(id: $id)




query {
  getBlogPost(id: 3) {
    id
    title
    isPrivate
    postPassword
    summary
  }
}


--> Đã lấy được mật khẩu của post có id=3.
articles.title: Lab: Accessing private GraphQL posts

articles.author: Kumar Kislay
articles.description:
TL;DR
Building a RAG-Native Knowledge Graph (Without the PhD)
To solve this, we moved beyond simple vector search and built a "Knowledge Graph" that maps the actual relationships between your tools.
Here is the 3-step process we use to turn scattered data into a queryable graph.
Step 1: The Unified Ingestion (Connect)
Code: GitHub/GitLab
Instead of just dumping text into a vector database, we ingest these as distinct Entities (e.g., a Commit, a Meeting, a Ticket).
Step 2: Automatic Context Linking (The "Graph" Part)
For example, if a Pull Request mentions "Ticket-123", we create a hard edge in the graph. But we go deeper:
Temporal Linking: "This meeting happened 10 minutes before this major commit."
Semantic Linking: "This Slack thread discusses the same 'Auth Bug' found in the Jira ticket."
This creates a Knowledge Graph where you can visually see connections between people, projects, and decisions.
Step 3: Graph-Based Retrieval (Query)
We traverse the graph:
Identify the Decision entity regarding the database.
The result? The user sees the meeting summary and the code PR side-by-side, answering the "why" instantly.
Conclusion
Building a graph sounds intimidating, but it's really just about respecting the relationships between your data. By connecting these dots automatically, we stop knowledge from walking out the door when a developer leaves.
articles.title: How We Architected Context: The Connect-Link-Query Pattern

June 4, 1996. After a decade of development and $7 billion in investment, the Ariane 5 rocket lifted off on its maiden voyage. 37 seconds later, it exploded.

This wasn't an obscure edge case. It was a predictable C language vulnerability that code review should have caught.

articles.author: Matsuzaki Yosuke
articles.description:
Hello devs!
To visualize the invisible manual labor of coding, I built a desktop widget using Rust and Tauri v2.
I did the math based on a standard mechanical switch actuation force (80g):
1 Keystroke = 80g
1 Day of Coding = ~500kg (1.7 Grand Pianos) 🎹
I realized I was lifting a car every week with just my fingers. No wonder my wrists hurt.

This was the most interesting technical decision.
rdev). However, I chose a low-level polling strategy (checking key states every 50ms) for this tool.
Why?
 Stability: Hooks can crash the input chain if they bug out. Polling is isolated.
 Permission Hell: macOS requires intrusive "Input Monitoring" permissions for hooks. Polling bypasses some of this friction.
 Privacy: I only needed to know if a key is pressed to calculate the "weight", not which key was pressed.
It’s a tradeoff: I sacrificed nanosecond precision for rock-solid stability.
I implemented a "Health Bar" system that drains as you type, treating coding energy like HP in a video game.

If you are curious about the implementation or want to see your own "Daily Tonnage", I've put the tool up here.
The Burnout Meter (booby.dev)
(It's free and runs locally, no data is sent to the cloud)
Have you ever dealt with RSI? I'd love to hear your thoughts.
articles.title: Rust vs RSI: How I calculated that I lift 500kg/day with my fingers
